unharnessed.meaning: Every beat is kept: the bald question, the portrait, the reading list, "$1.12 of last month's allowance", the geometry report, the Texas Freshman, the telegram P.S. Nothing invented.
unharnessed.sense: Terms fit: "verandah roof" for porch roof, "crabby old thing" for snappy, "chock-a-block" for cluttered corridors, "a bit odd" for queer (the period sense), "what she's on about".
unharnessed.authenticity: Light, natural Australian: "I've got four on the go at once", "mind", "Turns out". "Hooroo, Daddy" is genuine but a touch stagey in a girl's letter; otherwise unforced.
unharnessed.register: A level-2 touch: everyday Aussie phrasing ("chock-a-block", "staying back too") without pub-yarn slang, and no swearing, matching vulgarity 0.
unharnessed.tone: Judy's breathless, cheeky, eager voice survives: "Oh, you see, I know! You're a crabby old thing with a temper on you." The mock-formal "I have the honour to report" is kept.
unharnessed.flow: Reads smoothly except one clumsy doubling: "a sort of sprinkly grey sort of hair".
unharnessed.variety: Spread of light terms ("verandah", "chock-a-block", "on the go", "left by the wayside", "Hooroo") with no tic repeated.
unharnessed.essence: Unmistakably the Daddy-Long-Legs letter: the interrupted diary structure, the bells, the self-mocking ignorance list all intact.

yarn.meaning: All points kept, including the portrait, the list of books, the geometry report and the telegram P.S. "I'm pretty rapt with it" renders "very satisfactorily" faithfully.
yarn.sense: Mostly exact ("rapt", "chock-a-block", "fit to burst"), but "a straight line that's keen to turn down" strains "tendency", and "the only girl at uni" swaps an American women's college for an Aussie "uni"; "switch on the brass student lamp" loses the lighting of a period lamp.
yarn.authenticity: Natural Aussie: "rapt", "mates", "heaps more", "Chrissie". "a great big hole of not-knowing" is a forced paraphrase rather than how anyone talks.
yarn.register: Light everyday Aussie at about level 2 ("rapt", "mates", "Chrissie"), no swearing.
yarn.tone: Lively and cheeky, but a little more modern-casual than Judy ("here's the thing: do I give you some hair or not?", "a real oddball"), which nudges the period charm.
yarn.flow: Smooth overall; "a great big hole of not-knowing my brain is" is a clunky stretch.
yarn.essence: Clearly the original, though "uni" and the modernised phrasing pull it slightly out of its 1910s American college.

engine.meaning: Essentially the original text with spelling changes, so every point survives.
engine.sense: The few changes fit: "verandah roof", "heaps of others", "merry Chrissie".
engine.authenticity: What Aussie there is sounds fine, but US forms are left standing beside it: "bath robe", "in vacation", "Good-by", "have your secretary telegraph"; "merry Chrissie" is bolted onto otherwise untouched prose.
engine.register: Largely untranslated: apart from "verandah", "heaps", "colour"/"realising" and "Chrissie", it is the original word for word, lighter than a level-2 brief.
engine.tone: The tone is the original's, intact.
engine.variety: Only three or four Aussie touches in the whole letter.
engine.essence: Unmistakably the original, since it is nearly unchanged.

summaries.unharnessed: A clean, light level-2 retelling that keeps every detail and Judy's voice; only a small repetition and one slightly stagey sign-off.
summaries.yarn: Lively, natural light Aussie with good finds ("rapt", "fit to burst"), but a few strained or modernising choices.
summaries.engine: Faithful but barely translated; a spelling pass plus a few words, short of the level-2 brief.
